title: How Language Models Learn Taste: Brand Preference in LLMs
abstract: arXiv:2610.28272v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Asked to name a running shoe brand, language models say Nike. Asked to recommend one, they say Brooks. This paper asks where models learn that taste. Across 102 models and 42 brand categories, the brand a model picks when recommending differs from the brand it names in 26. The field moves together to a shared recommendation. The Named brands are market leaders, and the Picked brands are mostly niche and specialist. Three open training pipelines show where this forms. Pretraining already attaches the recommended brand to advice. Supervised fine-tuning teaches the model to answer and mostly leaves the pick unchanged. Preference optimization (DPO) teaches the model which answer is better, and the pick moves in all three pipelines, by 11 to 24 points. The preference data contains almost no brands. translated_title: 语言模型如何习得品味：大语言模型中的品牌偏好
translated_abstract: 当被要求说出一个跑鞋品牌时，语言模型会回答耐克；当被要求推荐一个时，它们却会推荐Brooks。本文探究模型从何处习得这种品味。在102个模型和42个品牌类别中，模型推荐时选择的品牌与其说出的品牌在26个类别中存在差异。整个领域共同趋向于一致的推荐。被说出的品牌是市场领导者，而被推荐的品牌大多是小众和专业品牌。三个开放的训练流程揭示了这种偏好的形成过程：预训练阶段就已经将推荐的品牌与建议行为关联起来；监督微调教会模型如何作答，但基本不改变其推荐选择；偏好优化（DPO）则教会模型哪个答案更好，在所有三个流程中，推荐选择都发生了11到24个百分点的偏移。值得注意的是，偏好数据中几乎不包含任何品牌。即使偏好的品牌并未出现在偏好数据中，DPO也会使模型的判断向另一组关联偏移，且这种效应持续存在。
tldr: 语言模型在“说出品牌”时倾向市场领导者，而在“推荐品牌”时却偏向小众专业品牌，这种品味形成于预训练并被DPO偏好优化显著放大，即使偏好数据中几乎不含品牌信息。
en_tdlr: LLMs name market-leading brands but recommend niche, specialist ones; this "taste" emerges during pretraining and is amplified by DPO preference optimization, even when brands are nearly absent from the preference data.
